body:
The `NoInfer` type appears to be responsible for the current strange behavior.

With the current implementation: `Exclude<NoInfer<R>, undefined>;`

```ts
type ExcludeUndefined<R> = Exclude<NoInfer<R>, undefined>;

let n1: ExcludeUndefined<number | undefined> = undefined;     // ok
let n2: ExcludeUndefined<Number | undefined> = undefined;     // not excluded
let s1: ExcludeUndefined<string | undefined> = undefined;     // ok
let s2: ExcludeUndefined<String | undefined> = undefined;     // not excluded
let d1: ExcludeUndefined<Date | undefined> = undefined;       // not excluded
let arr1: ExcludeUndefined<number[] | undefined> = undefined; // not excluded
let obj1: ExcludeUndefined<{} | undefined> = undefined;       // ok
let null1: ExcludeUndefined<null | undefined> = undefined;    // ok
```
https://www.typescriptlang.org/play/?#code/C4TwDgpgBAogHgYwDYFcAmECqA7DAzAS2wjQB4AlAPigF5ZFUNSA5AewEls8IAnCygDRQUuCIWJpKAbgBQMpBGBRsARgBc9ZOiyjxJUthQBbAEa8oAH2G6iJanRH5baKVDduA9B6isA1vMVlACYNeC0MHCcJFmMzHktrKLtaRLFnV3coL2VWJQgGbTQApQBndU1GHSSyEuAeIgBzBMc0iXtUvRdMrO8-YqgSkIrtSNb9AGU6xuabNpSWzoz3bOxcqHzwkn60crDK0c7SABEAQ2BoKwXndquJJcyVtY3KooUlE54eXYKI2f1DUy8ADaAF0ZtUbn8uo88j8tm8fCYAFbfTYHZykADeAF9wWNJPMofdlr1-AjDEgkKj9lCDChKXjOpDqvdsn0gA

Without `NoInfer`: 

```ts
type ExcludeUndefined<R> = Exclude<R, undefined>;

let n1: ExcludeUndefined<number | undefined> = undefined;     // ok
let n2: ExcludeUndefined<Number | undefined> = undefined;     // ok
let s1: ExcludeUndefined<string | undefined> = undefined;     // ok
let s2: ExcludeUndefined<String | undefined> = undefined;     // ok
let d1: ExcludeUndefined<Date | undefined> = undefined;       // ok
let arr1: ExcludeUndefined<number[] | undefined> = undefined; // ok
let obj1: ExcludeUndefined<{} | undefined> = undefined;       // ok
let null1: ExcludeUndefined<null | undefined> = undefined;    // ok
```

https://www.typescriptlang.org/play/?#code/C4TwDgpgBAogHgYwDYFcAmECqA7DAzAS2wjQB4AlAPigF5ZFUMKAaKFXCQ4tSgbgCh+SCMCjYAjAC56ydFg5cSpbCgC2AIwgAnKAB82CoiWp12+I2l5Rr1gPS2oAewDWQkWIBM0+LIw5z3KQAcmqaOvpmnBYmBgEkVjZQ9k6uwqIAzlIyjPJxZOnAWkQA5nqxUdwxkYqWiUkOLm4ZXtly-hVKAMqFJWXV0bTlNQk2yY1pUGhZPjntNaQAIgCGwNARhpWD-dwjiWOp7ktaWtMMbRtKKhraANoAun0XPFtPVvtNTuoAVqe+uR1kADeAF9Hnkqq86nYGgdRCokEhfrMnsoUAiwQCIXldu8gA
This looks like an upstream issue with Infer, I've filed microsoft/TypeScript#60594 to track it.
In the meantime, would it be possible to temporarily remove the NoInfer to make sure the loader does not have the undefined type? I feel it is hurting more than helping given this issue exists...
switching from `Exclude<NoInfer<R>, undefined>` to `NoInfer<Exclude<R, undefined>>` seems to resolve the issue

issue.body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

core

### Description

Not sure this is the correct place to provide some feedback about the resource API, but here it is:

1. I would love to be able to type narrow the value() type in the template (and outside too) to get rid of undefined type when verifying hasValue or if status is resolved, unless I would explicitly add undefined to the generic type. I am not sure this is possible, but it would be great.

2. when providing a request function to a resource, I would have expected the function to possibly return undefined, but not inside the loader as it should type narrow it because loader only runs if request does not return undefined.

### Proposed solution

1. In the template, if under a condition of status is equal to resolved, do not union undefined in return type of value()
2. in a resource, within loader function, request should not have undefined as a possible return type.

### Alternatives considered

Stay as is

issue.body: `httpResource` is a new frontend to the `HttpClient` infrastructure. It declares a dependency on an HTTP endpoint. The request to be made can be reactive, updating in response to signals for the URL, method, or otherwise. The response is returned as an instance of `HttpResource`, a `WritableResource` with some additional signals which represent parts of the HTTP response metadata (status, headers, etc).
